Access Management and Security

Authentication, RBAC roles, API keys, OAuth, SSL/TLS, and secrets management

Ops Guide — 6 of 6

Authentication — Three Methods

AI Mentor supports three authentication methods. The system checks them in priority order: if a valid token of higher priority is found, the remaining methods are not checked.

Request
API Key present?
Yes
API Auth
No
JWT Bearer present?
Yes
JWT Auth
No
JWT Cookie present?
Yes
Cookie Auth
No
401 Unauthorized
MethodFormatTransportPurposePriority
API Keyipx_...Header: Authorization: Bearer ipx_...MCP and programmatic integrations1 (highest)
JWT tokenJWTHeader: Authorization: Bearer eyJ...Programmatic clients2
JWT cookieJWTCookie: access_tokenBrowser SPA3

Check order: API Key → JWT header → JWT cookie. If the request contains a Bearer token with the ipx_ prefix, the system recognizes it as an API key and verifies it against the hash in the database. Otherwise, it attempts to decode it as a JWT. If the header is absent, it checks the access_token cookie.

API Key Storage API keys start with the ipx_ prefix and are stored in the database as a SHA-256 hash. Even in the event of a database leak, the keys cannot be recovered.

RBAC — Roles and Permissions

The access model is built on Role-Based Access Control. Tenants (users) are assigned to roles via the TenantRole table. Each role contains a JSON field permissions with three sections:

SectionTypeDescriptionMerge Rule
featuresBoolean flagsEnable/disable featuresOR — any True wins
limitsNumeric limitsQuantitative restrictionsMAX — the highest value wins
chat_contextChat contextAllowed query typesUNION — union of allowed_query_types

If a tenant has multiple roles, permissions are merged according to the rules above. This means that adding any role can only expand access, never restrict it.

Key Features

FeatureDescription
adminAccess to the admin panel
documents.uploadAbility to upload documents
chat.useUse the web chat

Key Limits

LimitDescription
max_productsMaximum number of products per tenant
max_documents_per_productMaximum documents per product
max_file_size_mbMaximum uploaded file size

Access checks in FastAPI use dependencies: require_email_verified requires a confirmed email, require_admin requires a role with features.admin = true. They are attached to endpoints via Depends().

API Keys

API keys are created in the admin panel or via the API. Each key is stored in the database with the following fields:

FieldDescription
key_hashSHA-256 hash of the key (the key itself is not stored)
tenant_idBound to the owning tenant
is_activeWhether the key is active
last_used_atLast usage timestamp

Revoking a key: set is_active = false in the admin panel or via the API. The key stops working immediately — no restart is needed.

Check key usage in the databasedocker exec ai-mentor-postgres-1 psql -U ai_mentor -d ai_mentor -c "SELECT id, tenant_id, is_active, last_used_at FROM api_keys ORDER BY last_used_at DESC LIMIT 10;"
Auditing unused keys The last_used_at field is updated with every request — convenient for auditing unused keys.

OAuth Providers

AI Mentor supports sign-in via Google and GitHub. Both providers are configured through environment variables in .env:

ProviderClient IDClient Secret
GoogleGOOGLE_CLIENT_IDGOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
GitHubGITHUB_CLIENT_IDGITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET

Users who sign in via OAuth automatically receive email_verified = true — email confirmation is not required.

APP_BASE_URL is required The APP_BASE_URL variable must be set correctly (e.g., https://ai-mentor.ru) — it is used to construct the redirect URI during OAuth authorization. An incorrect value → OAuth will not work.

SSL/TLS

TLS is terminated at Nginx. Certificates and keys are stored on the host:

FilePath
Certificate (fullchain)/etc/nginx/ssl/ai-mentor.ru.fullchain.pem
Private key/etc/nginx/ssl/ai-mentor.ru.key
ParameterValue
ProtocolsTLS 1.2, TLS 1.3
HSTSEnabled (Strict-Transport-Security)
X-Content-Type-Optionsnosniff
X-Frame-OptionsDENY
Check certificate expiration dateopenssl x509 -in /etc/nginx/ssl/ai-mentor.ru.fullchain.pem -noout -dates
Certificate renewalcp /path/to/new/fullchain.pem /etc/nginx/ssl/ai-mentor.ru.fullchain.pem cp /path/to/new/privkey.pem /etc/nginx/ssl/ai-mentor.ru.key nginx -t && nginx -s reload
Monitor certificate expiration dates. When they expire, the site will become inaccessible over HTTPS. Check dates regularly and renew in advance.

Secrets Management

SecretPurposeHow to Generate / ObtainIf Leaked
JWT_SECRET_KEYJWT token signingopenssl rand -hex 32All sessions are invalidated
GEMINI_API_KEYLLM API accessGoogle AI StudioQuota abuse
POSTGRES_PASSWORDDatabase accessSet in .envFull database access
API_KEYStatic legacy keySet in .envAPI access
RESEND_API_KEYEmail delivery serviceResend dashboardEmail spoofing
All secrets are stored in /opt/ai-mentor/.env on the VPS. This file is NOT in git. Access is restricted to root only. Never commit secrets to the repository.

MCP Security

The MCP server uses McpApiKeyAuthMiddleware for authentication. Each request must contain a Bearer token with the ipx_ prefix.

ParameterValue
MiddlewareMcpApiKeyAuthMiddleware
Allowed hostsai-mentor.ru, localhost, 127.0.0.1
LoggingEvery request is recorded in the mcp_request_log table

The mcp_request_log table provides a full audit trail: which key, which tool, timestamp, and request parameters. Useful for debugging and monitoring MCP usage.

Recent MCP requestsdocker exec ai-mentor-postgres-1 psql -U ai_mentor -d ai_mentor -c "SELECT created_at, tool_name, api_key_id FROM mcp_request_log ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20;"
